draft.title: Just in time
card: Just in time (JIT) is a way of managing inventory. Materials and parts arrive only when they are needed for production, not weeks before.
The business holds very little stock. This cuts storage costs such as warehouse space, and it frees up money that would be tied up in unused stock.
JIT depends on suppliers delivering on time, every time. If a supplier is late, production can stop because there is no spare stock to use.
A business using JIT needs a close, reliable relationship with its suppliers and careful planning of when materials are due.
draft.remember: JIT trades lower storage costs for greater exposure to supplier delays.

a.q: Which change would a business most likely see after moving to JIT?
opts: Lower storage costs, but a greater risk from late deliveries
Higher storage costs, but a lower risk from late deliveries
Lower storage costs, and no risk from late deliveries
Higher storage costs, and a greater risk from delays
a.why: JIT means little stock is held, so storage costs fall. With no spare stock, a late delivery can stop production, so the risk rises. The option claiming no risk is wrong because the business has nothing to fall back on.
a.clue: Think about what happens to stock levels, and what is left if a delivery fails.

b.q: Priya runs a furniture workshop in Newcastle and uses JIT for timber. A timber delivery arrives two days late. Why does this hurt her business more than a business holding large stocks?
opts: She has no spare timber, so production may have to stop
She must pay extra to store the timber that did arrive
She has to value her stock using LIFO instead of FIFO
She has lost the savings on warehouse space she made
b.why: JIT keeps stock very low, so a late delivery leaves no timber to keep working with and production can stop. Storage costs are not the problem here, because JIT cuts them, and the warehouse savings are not lost by one late delivery.
b.clue: Ask what she can use while she waits for the delivery.

a.best: Lower storage costs, but a greater risk from late deliveries

b.best: She has no spare timber, so production may have to stop
